pairs.why: A has the chunky, simplified planks and posts and the plain stylized water of the real pier; B goes toward realistic water caustics and a wide, detailed beach scene.
A's three-quarter view with the cap off-center and its soft satin sheen matches the real ball more closely; B is a flatter, front-on version.
B is close-cropped and plain like the real viewer, with blue and silver metal; A adds props, a mirror-reflective lens and a cartoon 'face' that reads more toy-like.
Both get the white keys wrong (the real keys are navy), but A's matte-satin body and crisper key shapes sit nearer the real finish than B's puffier, glossier version.
B's canopy panels are slightly puffier and more pillowy, like the real umbrella; the two are otherwise nearly the same.
B matches the real card's plain unit on a muted striped wall with soft airflow; A adds room props, a glowing light strip and oversaturated color.
A's thick rope with a soft twist has the smooth, chunky finish of the real cards; B's fine-stranded rope is the too-texture-y look the lessons reject.
Texture is similar, but A's coil with a running loop is built like a real lasso, while B has a strange knot where the loops join.
